results.evidence: Both fields are true of different parts of the line: the Napeequa approach traverses north of the Pilz Glacier beneath the north ridge into the upper basin, then gains the ridge by a scree gully near 8,000 ft, and the finish is an easy scramble up the southeast ridge. results.fact: Climbing season: 'May-Jun' header vs. a season description running through September
results.evidence: Every documented ascent of this line found is late May / early June: a Memorial Day (May 28-30) ascent via the south slope-southwest face and a June 1, 2025 ascent via Thunder Creek, the latter timed so the snow had melted off the summit while the steep sections still took crampons; a November attempt failed on wind-loaded snow. No source documents a mid/late-summer or September ascent, or states that the face becomes a dry scramble in summer, so neither the 'May-Jun' chip nor best_season/climate's 'through September' can be confirmed by two sources. No patch.
